Messages.Author: Ian Lee
Messages.Body:
>I finally got my first Derange! And -- what's the big deal? So you
>make a Vampire into a Malk Antitribu.

There are combos, but ignoring those, at superior, they slow decks down. Now,
that doesn't sound so bad, but unlike a number of other cards which do much the
same, it only goes away if you burn the vampire it's on, though having it on a
torpored vamp who will never get much is close to getting rid of it - just
lingers to annoy everyone except the owner who in all likelihood is completely
immune.

In far too many situations, it ends up being a lot like Sensory Dep. It's yet
another encouragement to play weenies since you can afford to have those
screwed with.

Also, Cam titled vampires lose their titles when they go Sabbat. As many vote
decks lack stealth or combat, it's often a pain to get it off of the, formerly,
titled vamp.

Messages.Author: Steve Wieck
Messages.Body:
Everything remains on schedule for us to receive the Sabbat War reprint the
middle of this month. I would expect it will be in retail stores world-wide
by the very end of January.

Vampire's relaunch has been successful due primarily to all of your efforts
to let retailers know this game is in demand. Sabbat War's first printing
sell-out (which green lighted Final Nights and a 3rd expansion) has all been
due to everyone working with their retailers and getting each retailer
excited about carrying the game. With a hoard of me-too Pokemon CCGs
flooding the market, it remains as important as ever to win retailers over
to Vampire - one retailer at a time. If you want more Sabbat War with this
new printing, please once again call or visit your favorite game retailer(s)
and let them know you want the product ordered. Placing pre-orders with your
retailer is even better for them and better insures product availability for
you.

>

> 2/15, but only the boosters. I hope this does not indicate that only
> the boosters will be reprinted. Can anyone ease my mind?

Both Starters and Boosters are being printed. 2/15 is late, I imagine
Potomac will revise this date soon.

Thanks All,

Steve Wieck

??? I'll try to explain the history the best that I can. This may be a bit
extraneous but...

Originally there was Jyhad (the first, "Limited" edition). I *think* VTES next
came out (not completely sure on this one). What they basically did was pull a
few cards out, add a few new cards in, try to make the rules clearly, etc. and
also change the backs of the cards. (VTES is kind of like a 2nd Edition and is
called "Unlimited," though it is much scarcer than the overproduced Jyhad).
Thus Jyhad and VTES (focusing solely only Camarilla) are more or less the base
set.

The first expansion was Dark Sovereigns (which "focused" on the Independent
Giovannia and Ravnos, though there were plenty of Cam stuff). The second
expansion was Ancient Hearts (similar to DS but "focusing" on Assamites and
Followers of Set).

The next thing was the Sabbat which was a stand-alone expansion (which means
you could play decks that were exclusively Sabbat). Sabbat was the last thing
printed by WotC and happened many years ago.

Since all that stuff happened so long ago, Sabbat War is the first "new"
expansion (but 4th expansion overall), focusing on the Sabbat clans. (Thus we
already have something Sabbat related). Because SW did so well, a second "new"
expansion (5th expansion overall) called Final Nights has been confirmed. Final
Nights is NOT Sabbat related -- it's supposed to boost the Independents.

So what Mr. Wieck is saying is that b/c SW did so well, a 3rd "new" expansion
(making it the 6th overall expansion) has been green-lighted, though we don't
know anything about it. It makes sense for it to do something with the
Camarilla (for the sake of the new players), but it's anyone's guess.

Halcyan 2
